name: themeguard
description: Audits a project's CSS colour variables: value collisions between roles, dead tokens, ramps that collapse between themes, and families a theme tunes everywhere except the members it silently inherits.

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build

//: 0.1.0 is the first release with something to run: `themeguard <file.css>` audits a stylesheet from a terminal, and the library is importable via the exports map. The tarball ships dist/ only — src/ and tests/ (including the 96 KB vendored calibration fixture) are development assets and stay out of it. 0.1.1 adds the optional themeguard.config.json, discovered beside the stylesheet, for marking specific findings deliberate. 0.1.2 lets an entry scope what it suppresses: a `tokens` set the finding must carry in full (a deliberate pair as ONE entry), and a `theme` narrowing the entry to findings measured in that theme — printed as [theme: …] / [tokens: …] on the suppressed line. 0.1.3 says WHERE: collision, scale-collapse and family-consistency findings now carry `sites` — the declaration each measured token resolved from — and end their message with it (`Declared at lines 41 and 33.`), citing the cascade winner rather than every place the name is written; dead-token, which already named `:root:402`, is unchanged. 0.1.4 adds the site-scoped half of suppression: a `/* themeguard-ignore <rule> [--token …] -- <why> */` comment in the stylesheet itself — trailing on the judged declaration or standalone on the line above — suppresses only findings living at its site, so a refactored defect re-reports instead of being held down by a judgement recorded elsewhere, and the report's suppressed section prints the directive's `[file:line]` source clause. 0.1.5 adds the report's `unmatched (N)` section — the complement of `suppressed`: every declared suppression that matched NOTHING, named with its rule, scope, source and reason, printed even at zero, never moving the exit code — so a judgement that has outlived its defect (or never aimed at one) can announce that instead of going silent. 0.1.6 adds the fifth rule, `unresolved-reference`: a `var()` naming a custom property that NO scope declares — a typo'd use, a fallback pointing at nothing, a declaration built on a name nobody wrote, or a `@theme inline` alias chain into a typo — which today passes green while the property falls back to unset/inherit or to the written fallback. One predicate over the references the parser already collects: one finding per name with every use site listed, `@theme inline` declarations count as declaring, suppression entries and themeguard-ignore directives target it through the same rule-id door, and it moves the exit code like any finding. 0.1.7 takes one invocation over several stylesheets: `themeguard a.css b.css` audits each file independently — the config beside each governs it, references do not cross files — and aggregates the per-file outcomes into one exit with the precedence 2 > 1 > 0, fail-fast on the first file that cannot be audited, so a CI or pre-commit caller gets one invocation and one verdict. 0.1.9 adds the sixth rule, `cycle-reference`: a `var()` loop — per CSS custom-property semantics every property in the loop, and every `var()` consuming a member, is invalid at computed-value time, yet the shape audits green because `dead-token` sees both names referenced and `unresolved-reference` sees both declared. One finding per (loop set, author) over the resolver's existing `kind:"cycle"` chains — no parse or resolve change: a loop authored outside any theme's own block (the base `:root` declarations, or the `@theme inline` alias namespace) is one `theme: null` finding, a loop a theme's own declarations close is a theme-scoped finding, and a theme that merely inherits a root-authored loop never re-reports it; the message names the loop as written, cites the cascade-winner declaration lines, and states the consequence. 0.1.11 lets a config judgement name the stylesheet it was recorded against: an optional `file` on a suppression entry, relative to the config's own directory and strictly validated (absolute, empty or non-string exits 2 naming the entry), resolved by the CLI before matching — a file-scoped entry governs that one stylesheet, so a directory sharing one config among sibling stylesheets can record a judgement for tokens.css without it silencing buttons.css; an entry without the field is byte-identical to 0.1.7, and an unmatched file-scoped entry now prints ` [file: …]` and a carve-out in the unmatched prose: for it, the report CAN tell — the judgement aims at the sibling the clause names, and that file's report states its fate.
